cards.front: Massive PE with persistent hypotension: systemic 100 mg alteplase IV over [___] hours.
cards.context:
Massive PE = obstruction killing the patient haemodynamically (sustained hypotension or vasopressor need despite fluid).

Alteplase 100 mg over 2 h is standard; in cardiac arrest from suspected PE, 50 mg bolus + continue CPR 60-90 min.

cards.front: Holliday-Segar daily electrolyte requirements: Na+ is 3 mmol per 100 mL of water, and K+ is [___] mmol per 100 mL.
cards.context:
Daily electrolyte requirements per Holliday-Segar: Na+ = 3 mmol per 100 mL of water requirement. K+ = 2 mmol per 100 mL.

For 70 kg: water = 2500 mL (25 units of 100 mL), so Na+ = 75 mmol/day, K+ = 50 mmol/day.

cards.front: Empiric bacterial meningitis in adults >50 (Australian guidelines): ceftriaxone 2g IV 12-hourly, dexamethasone before or with first dose, plus [___] 2g IV 4-hourly for Listeria cover.
cards.context:
Australian eTG empiric regimen: ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h covers Strep pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae.

Add ampicillin 2 g IV q4h for Listeria in patients >50, immunocompromised, alcoholic, or pregnant — ceftriaxone misses this intracellular organism.

Dexamethasone 10 mg IV q6h, given before or with the first antibiotic dose, cuts neurological complications (especially hearing loss) — it must precede antibiotic-triggered lysis.

cards.front: CT sensitivity for gallstones is only approximately [___]%, making ultrasound the preferred first-line imaging.
cards.context:
Ultrasound has >95% sensitivity for gallbladder stones and is first-line imaging. CT has poor sensitivity for gallstones (approximately 75%) because many stones are radiolucent.

Plain AXR detects only 10-15% of gallstones (the minority that are radio-opaque).

cards.front: The default maintenance IV fluid for a euvolaemic patient with normal electrolytes is 0.18% NaCl + [___]% glucose.
cards.context:
The default maintenance fluid for a euvolaemic patient with normal electrolytes is 0.18% NaCl + 4% glucose. It provides 31 mmol/L Na+ (appropriate for maintenance needs) plus glucose to prevent ketosis.

0.9% NaCl and Hartmann's are resuscitation fluids with too much Na+ for maintenance.

cards.front: Normal phosphate (PO₄) range is [___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
PO₄ 0.8-1.5 mmol/L. Required for ATP, 2,3-DPG (oxygen unloading), and intracellular signalling.

Symptoms appear at <0.4: muscle weakness (including diaphragm — failure to wean), confusion, rhabdomyolysis. Hyperphosphataemia (>1.5) reflects renal failure or tumour lysis.

cards.front: After treating anaphylaxis, observe for a minimum of 4 hours for a [___] reaction.
cards.context: Biphasic reactions occur in up to 20% of anaphylaxis cases. The second phase can be as severe as the first and typically occurs within 4-8 hours, which is why observation is mandatory.

cards.front: First-line imaging for suspected PE with Wells >4 and positive D-dimer is [___].
cards.context:
CTPA (CT pulmonary angiogram) directly visualises clot in the pulmonary arteries with sensitivity >95% and specificity >95%. It's the first-line definitive test in stable patients with Wells >4 (PE likely).

Bedside echo identifies RV strain in haemodynamically unstable patients (can't go to CT) — guides immediate thrombolysis decision.

cards.front: Severe exercise-associated hyponatraemia (EAH) with seizures: give 100 mL of [___] saline IV over 10 min.
cards.context: Severe EAH with encephalopathy is a medical emergency. The 100 mL bolus of 3% saline raises sodium by approximately 2-3 mmol/L — enough to reduce cerebral oedema without overcorrecting.

cards.front: First-line vasopressor in septic shock is [___].
cards.context:
Noradrenaline is the Surviving Sepsis Campaign first-line vasopressor — predominantly an α-1 agonist, raising MAP via vasoconstriction with modest β-1 inotropy.

Avoid dopamine (more arrhythmia, no survival benefit) and reserve adrenaline for refractory shock or anaphylaxis. Add vasopressin as the second agent at noradrenaline >0.25-0.5 mcg/kg/min.

cards.front: The restrictive transfusion threshold for stable ICU patients is Hb below [___] g/L.
cards.context:
Hb 70 g/L is the restrictive trigger from TRICC (Hebert 1999) — randomised trial showing restrictive (Hb <70) gave equivalent or better outcomes than liberal (<100) transfusion in stable ICU patients.

Lower Hb means fewer transfusion-related complications (TRALI, TACO, infection, immunomodulation).

Exceptions: active ACS or unstable angina (transfuse <80), active bleeding (transfuse by rate, not absolute number), and selected neurosurgical or cardiac patients where higher Hb is warranted.

cards.front: Digoxin Fab fragments are indicated for life-threatening [___] or potassium >5.5 mmol/L.
cards.context:
Digoxin toxicity kills via arrhythmia (VT, VF, CHB, junctional tachycardia) and hyperkalaemia from inhibited Na/K-ATPase shifting K out of cells — both findings drive Fab indication.

Fab (Digibind/DigiFab) binds digoxin as inert complexes cleared renally — expensive and limited stock, call pharmacy early.

cards.front: Post-arrest ABG targets? SpO₂: [___] (avoid hyperoxia). PaCO₂: 35–45 mmHg (normocapnia). Acidosis: treat the cause, not pH (bicarb only if pH < 7.1).
cards.context:
Post-ROSC hyperoxia worsens neurological outcomes via free radical injury. Hypocapnia reduces cerebral perfusion; hypercapnia increases ICP.

Bicarbonate generates CO₂ — rarely indicated unless pH below 7.1.

cards.front: F in FASTHUG BID = [___] (NOT fluids). Start enteral nutrition within 24-48 hours.
cards.context: Students reflexively say 'Fluids' because critically ill patients get lots of IV fluids.

cards.front: Empiric bacterial meningitis in adults >50 (Australian guidelines): [___] 2g IV 12-hourly, dexamethasone before or with first dose, plus ampicillin 2g IV 4-hourly for Listeria cover.
cards.context:
Australian eTG empiric regimen: ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h covers Strep pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae.

Add ampicillin 2 g IV q4h for Listeria in patients >50, immunocompromised, alcoholic, or pregnant — ceftriaxone misses this intracellular organism.

Dexamethasone 10 mg IV q6h, given before or with the first antibiotic dose, cuts neurological complications (especially hearing loss) — it must precede antibiotic-triggered lysis.

cards.front: Glucagon for beta-blocker overdose: [___] mg IV bolus, then 1-5 mg/hr infusion.
cards.context:
5-10 mg bolus is much higher than diabetic-emergency dose (1 mg) — receptor target is different.

Short-acting (half-life ~20 min) and rapidly depletes hospital stock — single severe BB overdose can exhaust supply in hours.

cards.front: Haemorrhagic shock Class III-IV requires [___], not just crystalloid.
cards.context: In haemorrhagic shock, crystalloid alone is insufficient for Class III and IV. These patients require blood products for volume and oxygen-carrying capacity.

cards.front: A patient develops acute dyspnoea, wheezing, urticaria, and hypotension during an infusion. Give [___] 0.5 mg IM.
cards.context: The clinical scenario of acute dyspnoea, wheezing, urticaria, and hypotension during an infusion is classic anaphylaxis.

cards.front: Ottawa Ankle Rules: X-ray if tenderness at posterior lateral or medial malleolus (distal 6 cm), base of 5th metatarsal, [___] bone, or unable to weight-bear 4 steps.
cards.context: The Ottawa rules check four bony areas plus weight-bearing ability. The midfoot component (base of 5th MT and navicular) is often forgotten but catches important fractures that can be missed clinically.

cards.front: For a paracetamol ingestion presenting early, the first nomogram level is drawn at [___] post-ingestion. NAC is started empirically if results are delayed beyond ~8 hours.
cards.context:
The Rumack-Matthew nomogram is calibrated from 4 hours post-ingestion onward — earlier samples haven't reached peak and may falsely reassure.

For an early presentation (2-8 hours), wait until 4 hours then plot. If the lab cannot return the level by 8 hours, start NAC empirically — delay sharply reduces efficacy.

The cost of unnecessary NAC is far lower than missed hepatotoxicity.

cards.front: GTN is contraindicated in chest pain when systolic BP is below [___] mmHg.
cards.context:
GTN contraindications: SBP <90 mmHg, RV infarct (preload-dependent), PDE5 inhibitor use within 24-48 hours. Always check BP before giving GTN.

In a hypotensive patient with chest pain, GTN will cause further vasodilation and haemodynamic collapse.

cards.front: SSC 2021 recommends [___] mL/kg of IV crystalloid in the first 3 hours of sepsis resuscitation.
cards.context: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 guidelines recommend 30 mL/kg in first 3 hours. Small boluses (250 mL at a time) are safer than large boluses, allowing reassessment between each.

cards.front: Vasopressin dose: fixed at 0.03 units/min. Not titrated due to narrow therapeutic window (risk: [___] ischaemia).
cards.context: Unlike catecholamines, vasopressin has a narrow therapeutic window — higher doses cause excessive vasoconstriction (gut ischaemia, digital ischaemia). The fixed dose provides benefit without the toxicity of escalation.

cards.front: Refractory anaphylaxis after repeated IM doses should be managed with a titrated IV adrenaline [___].
cards.context:
When two IM doses haven't restored perfusion, switch to titrated IV adrenaline infusion (1 mg of 1:1000 in 1 L = 1 µg/mL, run 1-10 mL/min, titrate to MAP ≥65).

The trap: IV bolus at the cardiac arrest dose (1 mg) in a perfusing patient causes tachyarrhythmia, hypertensive crisis, ischaemia. Move to infusion under continuous monitoring, pads on.
